items.title: BPCL outlines SAF work at FICCI summit: Mumbai ISCC CORSIA certification, Topsoe licence, Akasa MoU
items.text: BPCL's aviation head said its Mumbai refinery holds ISCC CORSIA certification for co-processing used cooking oil, and that BPCL has a technology licence from Topsoe for kerosene hydrotreating to enable renewable co-processing. Its July 2026 MoU with Akasa Air led to a 1% SAF-blended flight in September 2026. No volumes or offtake quantities were given, so earnings materiality stays unquantified.

items.title: Naidu: draft SAF policy to open for public consultation in 1-2 weeks; IOC Panipat cleared to supply
items.text: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu told the FICCI SAF Summit that the draft SAF policy awaits comments from the Petroleum Ministry and should go to public consultation within one to two weeks. It proposes a National Council, a DGCA-run National SAF Registry and public-private partnerships for feedstock. IOC Chairman A S Sahney said Panipat has government approval for commercial SAF supply, designed for about 35,000 tonnes a year from used cooking oil, enough to meet the 1% international-flight target in 2027. Targets cited are 1% (2027), 2% (2028) and nearly 5% (2030). Final policy and pricing remain pending.

items.title: Draft SAF policy still unapproved; minister denies ethanol-in-ATF plan, ATJ route stays in focus
items.text: The Week reported on 10 Nov 2026 that the draft National Policy on SAF has not received final approval. It sets international-flight blending at 1% (2027), 2% (2028), 3% (2029) and 5% (2030), with 2040 targets reported as 20% or 40%, and SAF costing two to three times conventional jet fuel. Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu called a claim that raw ethanol would be mixed into ATF 'completely false', and the April ATF Control Order amendment set no mandatory blend. Ethanol reaches jet fuel only via alcohol-to-jet processing, with cane molasses, syrup and surplus sugar named as feedstocks, which is relevant to Praj and sugar/distillery names; final pricing and support terms remain the open catalyst.
